chunks: And as for the right of hearing, it is to keep it pure from listening to backbiting, and listening to that to which it is unlawful to listen.

key_terms.الْغَيْبَةِ: Backbiting (speaking about someone in their absence)
key_terms.تَنْزِيهُهُ: To purify it / to keep it free from

ai.seo_question: What is the right of hearing in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin expands the concept of 'right of hearing' by distinguishing between the prohibition of backbiting (ghiba) and the broader obligation to avoid unlawful auditory inputs, reflecting the Shia emphasis on purifying the senses as a means of spiritual discipline. This instruction aligns with the jurisprudential principle that guarding one's faculties is a prerequisite for fulfilling the rights of Allah, ensuring that the heart remains receptive to divine guidance rather than distracted by trivial or corrupting sounds.
